recognize_zh: 紅血球背景中有一條細長、彎曲的蟲體，內部可見一列藍紫色細胞核（nuclear column），蟲體外有淡色的鞘（sheath），這是微絲蟲（microfilaria）的典型外觀；依病例說明為班氏絲蟲（Wuchereria bancrofti）。
features: Single elongated, gently undulating worm many times the length of a red cell, lying among erythrocytes
Body filled with a column of dark blue-purple somatic nuclei
Thin pale sheath-like outline running along the body
One end (left) is tapered and embedded in a purple amorphous/fibrinous clump, limiting assessment of tail-tip nuclei
Background of dense erythrocytes with scattered platelets; no specific host-cell reaction around the parasite
describe_en: Smear (reported as bone marrow aspirate, Jenner-Giemsa) shows a single elongated, sheathed microfilaria with a gently curved body lying among erythrocytes. The body contains a column of darkly staining somatic nuclei, and one end tapers within an amorphous purple fibrin-like clump. The tail tip and the distribution of terminal nuclei cannot be fully assessed at this magnification. Findings are consistent with a sheathed microfilaria, compatible with Wuchereria bancrofti in the appropriate clinical and geographic setting.

ddx.vs: Brugia is also sheathed but has a sheath staining pink with Giemsa, a kinked body, and two separate terminal nuclei at the tail tip, whereas W. bancrofti has smooth curves and no nuclei in the tail tip.
Loa loa is sheathed but its nuclear column extends continuously to the tip of the tail, and the sheath often stains poorly with Giemsa.
Mansonella microfilariae are smaller, unsheathed, and have nuclei extending to a blunt tail tip.
Artifacts lack an organized internal column of discrete nuclei and a defined tapered anterior and posterior end.
